messages:
emma: FYI — Received an urgent customer report: objects that should be preserved by a custom 90-day retention are showing as deleted/purged in search. Ticket 789321. They say they set custom retention on 2024-03-10.

raj: Can you paste one object ID and the API request the customer used to set the custom retention? Also want the small repro steps.

emma: Object IDs: obj_9f3a1c, obj_9f3a1d. Customer claim: POST /v1/retention with {\"policy\":\"cust-90d\", \"target\":[obj_9f3a1c,obj_9f3a1d]} on 2024-03-10. They got 200.

raj: Running quick check against metadata store now. If retention policy replaced by default due to migration, TTL might have been recomputed.

retention-bot: automated-check: no active legal hold found for obj_9f3a1c, last retention_update=171_740_8000, current_ttl=30d(default).

emma: retention-bot timestamp looks wrong — that key should have been set 2024-03-10 by customer.

david: I'm seeing a background migration ran 2024-03-09->2024-03-11 (index schema v3). There was a fallback script that backfilled missing retention_policy field with default=30d when the policy lookup failed. Need to check why policy lookup failed for these IDs.

mara: Legal flagged this as potential data-loss during a contractually required 90-day retention. Please treat as high priority. 

raj: Hypothesis: customer used a custom policy name that didn't exist in the new catalog during migration (cust-90d -> cust-90-day). The backfill fallback applied default. Need logs from the policy service and KMS audit to confirm.

emma: Customer also mentioned they attempted an export on 2024-03-15 and saw missing objects in the export. They can share the export job id if needed.

david: Requesting KMS/HSM logs for key used by the customer's org for 2024-03-09..2024-03-16. If the policy lookup required decrypting a policy blob and KMS calls failed, fallback could have triggered.

raj: Quick repro steps I'm running (internal):
```
# repro: simulate policy name mismatch and run backfill
python tools/retention_sim.py --org acme-corp --policy-name cust-90d --ids obj_9f3a1c,obj_9f3a1d
# check metadata
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj_9f3a1c/meta
```

emma: Customer called legal and is asking for ETA to restore visibility/export results. They want confirmation whether objects are actually purged from storage or only missing from index.

david: Storage layer shows tombstone marker present for obj_9f3a1c with deletion_epoch=171_741_0000. That suggests an index-level fallback triggered deletion pipeline. Need full audit log chain: retention write -> migration backfill -> delete job.

mara: Legal requests: 1) freeze any auto-purge for this org immediately, 2) produce audit log for retention policy changes on the account, 3) timeline of all automated jobs touching these objects.

raj: I'm putting an emergency prevent-purge flag on the org now (internal command). Also creating a canary to re-run export using raw storage reads to confirm presence.

retention-bot: action: prevent-purge flag applied by raj at 3012345690.

emma: I'll reply to the customer: we have applied a prevent-purge, investigating migration logs & KMS calls, aim to produce audit log & export in next 4 hours.

david: To-do list for infra: KMS audit (david), policy-service logs (david + raj), delete-job trace (raj), raw-storage export (raj).

mara: Also loop in compliance for longer-term preservation requirements if restore not possible.

raj: Update: repro shows policy lookup failed when policy name had hyphen vs underscore. Backfill script matched only exact names. I'll attach exact log lines in follow-up.

emma: Thanks — keep me posted. I'll update customer with interim status.

retention-bot: reminder: attach correlation_id from customer export to the ticket for faster lookup.

emma: Correlation id requested from customer: export_job_55f4.

(End of thread)
